mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved monotonically from -39.6% to -21.3% over four weeks, signaling sustained recovery momentum. This trend will continue, producing further gains over the next four weeks as the baseline effect compounds.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 18.3 percentage points over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains depressed and volatile (ranging -35.3% to -23.0%), indicating incomplete return-to-office. This persistent workplace suppression constrains daytime retail foot traffic, preventing RETAIL_REC recovery from accelerating beyond current levels.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -20% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has not exceeded -23.0% in any week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -15% in any single week during the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has stabilized near -54% to -58% over the last two weeks, indicating a floor in commuting suppression. If TRANSIT remains flat or rises modestly, it signals confidence in mobility resumption that will lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has narrowed from -66.0% to -54.1% over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT declines by more than 3 percentage points in the first two weeks of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC shows no improvement in week 1-2 of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has converged to near-baseline (-1.3%), indicating essential-trip normalization. Simultaneous RETAIL_REC recovery (-21.3%) suggests discretionary mobility is decoupling from essential mobility. If GROCERY_PHARM remains stable, RETAIL_REC will continue recovering as consumers shift to non-essential shopping.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM drops below -3% in any week during the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve relative to the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has been volatile (-8.4% to -14.6%) but remains suppressed, indicating outdoor-activity constraints persist. This suppression will lift RETAIL_REC as consumers substitute indoor retail for outdoor recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS has not risen above -6.4% in any week
failure_condition: PARKS rises above 0% in any week during the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from +16.0% to +8.4%, indicating reduced home-confinement pressure. This decompression, combined with TRANSIT stabilization, signals policy relaxation. Under relaxed restrictions, RETAIL_REC will accelerate over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines by more than 3 percentage points week-on-week AND TRANSIT improves by more than 2 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 7.6 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above +12% in any week during the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC shows no improvement in the first two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both severely suppressed (-23% to -54%), indicating a regime of restricted mobility. RETAIL_REC recovery will stall if both remain below their current levels, as the suppression regime persists and constrains all non-essential mobility.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT decline week-on-week in any two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain below -20%
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT rises by more than 8 percentage points in any single week, or RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved 18.3 points over four weeks while WORKPLACES remains depressed. This decoupling indicates consumers are shifting to retail despite workplace suppression, driven by pent-up demand. Over the next week, this demand will continue to drive RETAIL_REC gains as the effect is immediate.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC improves by more than 3 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 5.3 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in the first week of the forecast period, or the week-on-week improvement rate slows to less than 2 percentage points.
